subject: Human Evolution
title: The Descended Larynx
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Descended Larynx usable.

hook.text: In most mammals the larynx sits high, letting them breathe and swallow at the same time. Yours can't.

buildup.text: The human larynx dropped lower in the throat, creating a large resonating chamber above it.

discovery.text: That chamber lets us produce the wide vowel range needed for complex speech sounds.

twist.text: The trade-off is choking risk. Humans are the only primate that regularly chokes on food.

climax.text: Evolution accepted a deadly design flaw because the communication benefit outweighed the risk.

punchline.text: Speech was worth the choking hazard.

quiz.question: Why did the human larynx descend?
options: To create a vocal chamber for complex speech sounds
